itinerary.story:
Prague, known as the City of a Hundred Spires, rises like a medieval dream along the winding Vltava River. Its cobblestone labyrinth whispers tales of Bohemian kings, alchemists in dark towers, and the resilient spirit of a people who have preserved their architectural marvels through centuries of shifting empires. Every golden hour bathes the Gothic spires, Renaissance facades, and Baroque domes in a warm, timeless glow that has inspired artists and musicians for generations.

Walking across the mist-shrouded Charles Bridge at dawn, one can almost hear the echoes of footsteps from centuries past. The city's architectural layers are a tangible timeline, transitioning seamlessly from Romanesque rotundas to the soaring Gothic majesty of St. Vitus Cathedral, and finally to the whimsical curves of Art Nouveau buildings. It is a place where history is not confined to museums, but lives vibrantly in every courtyard, café, and shadowed alleyway.
itinerary.heritageSummary: Prague's historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage site that boasts an unmatched architectural tapestry spanning over a millennium. Celebrated for its Gothic, Baroque, and Cubist buildings, the city also maintains rich traditions in classical music, puppetry, and artisanal glassmaking. This heritage matters because it represents a living museum of Central European culture, where historical preservation coexists with a dynamic modern artistic community.

items.name: Prague Castle
items.blurb: The largest ancient castle complex in the world, serving as the historical seat of Czech rulers.
items.significance: Symbolizes the political and cultural heart of the Czech nation for over a thousand years.

items.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
items.blurb: A stunning Gothic masterpiece housing the tombs of Bohemian kings and the Crown Jewels.
items.significance: The spiritual heart of Prague and a pinnacle of European Gothic architecture.
items.bestTime: Late afternoon when sunlight hits the stained glass
items.geoQuery: St. Vitus Cathedral, Prague, Czech Republic

items.name: Golden Lane
items.blurb: A picturesque street of small, colorful houses originally built for the castle's guards.
items.significance: Offers a rare glimpse into the modest domestic scale of 16th-century castle life.

items.name: Vrtba Garden
items.blurb: An exquisite tiered Baroque garden tucked away on the slope of Petřín Hill.
items.significance: A masterpiece of Baroque landscape architecture offering panoramic views of the city roofs.

days.theme: Old Town Intrigue and Modernist Visions

items.name: Old Town Square
items.blurb: The historic public square featuring the iconic Astronomical Clock and pastel-colored burgher houses.
items.significance: The bustling commercial and social hub of medieval Prague.
items.geoQuery: Old Town Square, Prague, Czech Republic

items.name: Municipal House
items.blurb: A grand civic building showcasing breathtaking Art Nouveau architecture and interior design.
items.significance: A monument to the Czech National Revival and early 20th-century artistic excellence.

items.name: The House of the Black Madonna
items.blurb: A unique cubist building designed by architect Josef Gočár, now housing a museum and café.
items.significance: One of the world's few architectural examples of Cubism applied to building design.
items.geoQuery: House of the Black Madonna, Prague, Czech Republic

items.name: Grand Café Orient
items.blurb: The world's only Cubist interior café, complete with original furniture and chandeliers.
items.significance: Immerse yourself fully in Prague's brief, brilliant avant-garde Cubist design movement.
items.geoQuery: Grand Café Orient, Prague, Czech Republic

localSecrets.name: St. Agnes Monastery
localSecrets.blurb: The oldest Gothic monastic complex in Prague, now housing medieval art in tranquil surroundings.
localSecrets.significance: Brings visitors into a peaceful architectural oasis far away from the bustling tourist trails.
localSecrets.geoQuery: Convent of Saint Agnes of Bohemia, Prague, Czech Republic

localSecrets.name: Villa Amerika
localSecrets.blurb: A stunning High Baroque pavilion designed by Kilian Ignaz Dientzenhofer, currently a music museum.
localSecrets.significance: A hidden architectural gem showcasing the playful elegance of Czech Baroque design.

localSecrets.name: Nový Svět
localSecrets.blurb: A tiny, winding lane near the castle district with fairy-tale cottages and cobblestones.
localSecrets.significance: Preserves the secluded, rustic atmosphere of an old Prague suburb untouched by modern development.

events.name: Prague Spring International Music Festival
events.description: A prestigious celebration of classical music featuring world-renowned orchestras and soloists in historic venues.
events.culturalRoot: Honors the legacy of classical composition and performance deeply rooted in Czech cultural identity.

events.name: Signal Festival
events.description: A festival of light art that transforms historical facades, squares, and monuments with cutting-edge digital projections.
events.culturalRoot: Bridges Prague's historic architectural heritage with contemporary digital creativity.

events.name: Bohemia JazzFest
events.description: Open-air jazz concerts held in historic city squares across the Czech Republic, including prominent Prague locations.
events.culturalRoot: Celebrates the deep-seated Czech appreciation for improvisational and contemporary jazz music.

experiences.title: Traditional Marionette Puppet Workshop
experiences.description: Learn the intricate craft of string puppet manipulation and stagecraft from local artisan puppeteers.
experiences.howToEngage: Book a introductory puppet-making or manipulation workshop at specialized local theatres like Divadlo Spejbla a Hurvínka or independent studios.
experiences.respectfulTip: Approach the craft with patience and respect for the centuries-old tradition of Czech puppetry.

experiences.title: Architectural Sketching Walk
experiences.description: Explore the varied facades of Prague with a local architect, learning how to read Gothic, Baroque, and Cubist details.
experiences.howToEngage: Join a specialized guided walk organized by architectural preservation societies or local design centers.
experiences.respectfulTip: Do not block narrow pathways or doorways while sketching or taking architectural notes.

etiquette: Always greet shopkeepers and servers with 'Dobrý den' when entering a small shop or restaurant.
Remove your backpack in crowded trams and public transport to avoid bumping into others.
Keep your voice down when entering churches, monasteries, and quiet historical interiors.
Tipping around 10% is customary in sit-down restaurants if service is good, but check if service is included.
Always step to the right on escalators to allow people to walk up on the left.

hero.title: Prague
hero.extract: Prague is the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic and the historical capital of Bohemia. Located on the Vltava River, the city has a population of about 1.4 million, making it the twelfth-largest city in the European Union. Its metropolitan area is home to approximately 2.3 million people.

sources.title: Prague Castle
sources.extract: Prague Castle is a castle complex in Prague, Czech Republic serving as the official residence and workplace of the president of the Czech Republic. Built in the 9th century, the castle has long served as the seat of power for kings of Bohemia, Holy Roman emperors, and presidents of Czechoslovakia. As such, the term "Prague Castle" or simply "Hrad" are often used as metonymy for the president and his staff and advisors. The Bohemian Crown Jewels are kept within a hidden room inside it.

sources.title: St. Vitus Cathedral
sources.extract: The Metropolitan Cathedral of Saints Vitus, Wenceslaus and Adalbert is a Catholic metropolitan cathedral in Prague, and the seat of the Archbishop of Prague. Until 1997, the cathedral was dedicated only to Saint Vitus, and is still commonly named only as St. Vitus Cathedral.

sources.title: Old Town Square
sources.extract: Old Town Square is a historic square in the Old Town quarter of Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic. It is located between Wenceslas Square and Charles Bridge.
